117735.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Tidewater
117735.note: Jewish News (Tidewater), 22 Jan 2018: 'Chabad of Tidewater was founded 1979 under the leadership of the Lubavitcher Rebbe'; Rabbi Aaron Margolin is executive director. The paper's 'A Guide to Jewish Living in Tidewater' (9 Aug 2019) says the same: 'Established in 1979, Chabad Lubavitch of Tidewater...' (Chabad House, 1920 Colley Avenue, Norfolk).

118545.name: Chabad Tysons Jewish Center
118545.note: Connection Newspapers, 9 Sept 2003, 'Jewish Congregation Forms in Tysons': 'Started up by Levi Deitsch and his wife Miriam last September, Chabad at Tysons seeks to reach out to Jewish people'; 'The Deitsches moved to McLean from Brooklyn last May 2002'. Rabbi Levi Deitsch later passed away; his brother Rabbi Chezky (Yechezkiel) Deitsch came to help run it (CrownHeights.info) and directs it now.

564734.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Reston and Herndon
564734.note: Lubavitch.com on CrownHeights.info, 17 June 2007 (Chabad of Northern Virginia's 16th anniversary): 'A fourth center is scheduled to open this fall in the Western Fairfax area under the direction of Rabbi Laibel and Nechama Fajnland.' Its chabad.org listing went up 6 Sept 2007.

3588518.name: Chabad of Greater Gainesville & Manassas
3588518.note: CrownHeights.info, 12 Sept 2017, from the Prince William Times: 'Rabbi Shmuly Perlstein and his wife, Goldie Perlstein, have announced their plans to move to Gainesville to open the first Jewish Community Center in the area, Chabad Gainesville'; 'We've been visiting the greater Gainesville area over the last year'. Its chabad.org listing went up 30 Mar 2017.
